planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female selection needs a male hardy kiwi such as Issai or a hardy male clone growing nearby for pollination.

directions: 74-49, sometimes sold as Forty-Niner, is a female Actinidia arguta selection from a California breeding program prized for large, sweet, shiny green-to-reddish fruit that ripens earlier than many other hardy kiwi selections. Like all hardy kiwi, this is a dioecious vine and will not set fruit without a separate male vine planted within pollinating range. Provide a strong permanent trellis, as the twining vine is vigorous and long-lived, and expect several winters of establishment before heavy cropping begins. Vines tolerate cold well into zone 4 once established, though young plants benefit from winter protection.

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female Polish selection is one of the latest-ripening hardy kiwi cultivars and needs a male vine nearby for fruit set.

directions: Rogow is a prolific female hardy kiwi selected at the Warsaw University of Life Sciences arboretum in Rogow, Poland, bred for reliable cropping in a cold-continental climate. It produces small, oval, grape-sized berries with edible skin and good flavor, ripening notably late in the season, from late September into October. As a dioecious selection it requires a separate male Actinidia arguta vine planted within pollinating range to set fruit. The vigorous twining vine needs a strong permanent trellis and performs well in the same cold-hardy range as other named A. arguta cultivars.

common_name: Bingo Hardy Kiwi (WULS Poland Red-Blushed Kiwiberry Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female hybrid selection needs a separate male hardy kiwi vine nearby for pollination and fruit set.

directions: Bingo is a female hardy kiwi cultivar bred at Warsaw University of Life Sciences in Poland from a cross of Actinidia purpurea Purpurna Sadova and A. arguta, with fruit and vine characteristics dominated by its arguta parentage. The elliptical, laterally flattened fruit has smooth yellow-green skin with a strong rose-red blush and is rich in vitamin C with well-regarded flavor. As a dioecious vine, Bingo will not fruit without a compatible male hardy kiwi planted within pollinating range. Its Polish breeding origin gives it reliable cold hardiness for northern gardens on a sturdy, permanent trellis.

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; this female cultivar needs a hardy male kiwi or Issai nearby for pollination.

directions: Hardy Red is a female Actinidia arguta selection grown for cranberry-red-tinged skin and red-blushed flesh with a sweet, well-regarded flavor, distinguishing it from the mostly green-fruited hardy kiwi cultivars. Vines are vigorous twining climbers that need a strong permanent trellis or arbor and reliably tolerate winter temperatures down to around -25F. As with all Actinidia arguta, this is a dioecious cultivar and requires a separate male vine, such as a hardy male seedling or Issai, planted nearby to ensure fruit set. Expect a productive vine once established, ripening in fall alongside other hardy kiwi selections.

common_name: Red Princess Hardy Kiwi (Red-Fleshed New Zealand Kiwiberry Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female hybrid selection needs a separate male hardy kiwi vine planted nearby for fruit set.

directions: Red Princess is a New Zealand-bred female hardy kiwi selection, a cross of the Actinidia arguta type Cordifolia with A. melanandra, grown for smooth-skinned, oval, grape-sized fruit with striking red flesh and a sweet, concentrated kiwi flavor eaten whole without peeling. Fruit ripens mid to late fall, later than many arguta cultivars. Being dioecious, it requires a separate male hardy kiwi vine growing within pollinating range to set fruit. The vigorous vine is hardy to roughly -25F and needs a strong permanent trellis or arbor to support its twining growth.

common_name: Chang Bai Hardy Kiwi (Chinese Changbai Mountain Kiwiberry)

planting.note: Plant on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil in full sun; this female, late-flowering selection needs a male hardy kiwi vine nearby for pollination.

directions: Chang Bai is a female hardy kiwi selected near the Changbai Mountain region on the China-North Korea border, valued for productive, sweetly flavored, unusually apple- or heart-shaped green fruit. Originating from a cold, mountainous native range, it carries strong winter hardiness typical of Actinidia arguta selections from northern China. As a dioecious vine it will not fruit without a compatible male hardy kiwi planted nearby, and its late flowering allows pollination from either hardy arguta males or early-blooming fuzzy-kiwi males. Provide a sturdy permanent trellis for the vigorous twining growth habit.

common_name: Aromatnaya Kolomikta Kiwi (Sweet Aromatic Arctic Beauty Kiwi)

planting.note: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil; this female Russian-bred selection needs a male A. kolomikta vine nearby for pollination.

directions: Aromatnaya is a Russian-bred female Actinidia kolomikta selection producing medium-sized, very sweet, fragrant fruit on a vigorous and exceptionally productive vine, typically ripening in mid-August. Spring foliage on vigorous shoots shows the green, white, and pink variegation characteristic of the species, adding ornamental interest alongside the fruit crop. As with all kolomikta kiwi, this is a dioecious selection and requires a separate male vine planted within range for reliable pollination and fruit set. The species is exceptionally cold hardy, tolerating winter temperatures well below zero, making it a good choice for far northern gardens.

common_name: Pasha Male Arctic Beauty Kiwi (Ornamental Kolomikta Pollinator)

planting.note: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil as a pollinator vine; one Pasha male can pollinate several female Arctic Beauty kiwi vines if centrally located.

directions: Pasha is a male Actinidia kolomikta selection grown specifically as a pollinator for female Arctic Beauty kiwi vines, since the species is dioecious and female vines will not set fruit without a nearby male. Rather than producing fruit itself, Pasha is prized for its strikingly ornamental foliage, splashed with pink, white, and green variegation, making it an attractive vine in its own right on a trellis or arbor. It is exceptionally cold hardy, reportedly tolerating winter lows to around -40F, among the hardiest of all Actinidia selections. A single well-placed Pasha vine can pollinate multiple female kolomikta vines within range.

common_name: Frost Arctic Beauty Kiwi (Early-Ripening Variegated Kolomikta Kiwi)

planting.note: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil; this female selection needs a male A. kolomikta vine such as Pasha nearby for pollination.

directions: Frost is a female Actinidia kolomikta selection notable for bearing fruit unusually early after planting and ripening earlier in the season than most other kolomikta cultivars, typically in early to mid-August. It produces good crops of medium to large, bright green, very sweet fruit high in vitamin C, alongside foliage with distinct pink-edged variegation for ornamental appeal. As a dioecious vine it needs a separate male kolomikta selection, such as Pasha, planted within range for cross-pollination and fruit set. Like other kolomikta selections, it is exceptionally cold hardy, tolerating winter lows to around -40F.
